items.prompt: White to move. White already has a queen. Promote the pawn on c7 to a second queen.

claims.statement: The pawn may promote to a queen even though White already has one.

hints: Find the pawn and the last rank. Which square is straight ahead of it?
Having a queen already does not stop you: a pawn may become any of the four pieces.
Move the pawn one square forward and choose the queen.
items.explain: The pawn steps to the last rank and becomes a second queen. Owning a queen already does not limit the choice.

items.prompt: Black wants to promote the pawn on e2. Find the best way to do it.

claims.statement: Capturing the rook on d1 and promoting to a queen is the engine's best move.
Promoting straight ahead on e1 loses the new queen.

hints: A pawn can promote straight ahead or by capturing. Which promotion squares does this pawn have?
Check each promotion square: does an enemy piece attack it?
The rook on d1 watches the square straight ahead, but the rook itself can be captured.
items.explain: The rook on d1 attacks the square straight ahead, so a queen made there would be taken. Capturing the rook promotes the pawn and wins the rook at the same moment.

feedback_by_move.e2e1q: The queen appears on e1, but the rook on d1 attacks that square and takes it.

items.prompt: White to move. Tap every square where the pawn on d7 could land and promote.

claims.statement: The pawn can promote on d8 by moving ahead, or on c8 by capturing the rook.

hints: A pawn has up to three squares in front of it: straight ahead and the two diagonals.
Straight ahead needs an empty square. A diagonal needs an enemy piece standing on it.
Look at the three squares on the last rank: which is empty, which holds an enemy piece?
items.explain: Straight ahead is empty, so the pawn can move there. The rook stands diagonally ahead, so the pawn can capture it. The other diagonal square is empty, so there is nothing to capture there.

items.prompt: Black to move. Can the pawn on a2 promote on this move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The knight on a1 blocks the pawn.
The pawn cannot capture its own rook.

hints: Look at the square straight ahead of the pawn, then at the diagonal square.
A pawn moves straight only onto an empty square, and captures diagonally only an enemy piece.
One piece blocks the way ahead; whose colour is the piece on the diagonal?
items.explain: No. The white knight blocks the way ahead and a pawn cannot capture straight ahead. The diagonal square holds Black's own rook, and a pawn never captures its own piece.

items.prompt: Black to move. Can the pawn on g2 promote on this move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The pawn can capture the bishop on f1 and promote.
The rook on g1 blocks the straight move.

hints: Find the squares a black pawn on the second rank can reach on the last rank.
The square straight ahead holds a rook. What can a pawn do about a blocker?
Check both diagonal squares for an enemy piece.
items.explain: Yes, by capture. The rook blocks the way straight ahead, but the white bishop stands diagonally in front of the pawn, so the pawn can take it and promote.
